subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently remove `antml:`/`mm:`-qualified invoke XML from durable assistant history as well as visible replies, accepting that an intentional qualified XML example cannot be recovered?
rationale: The code can reliably distinguish bare and Markdown-code examples, but it cannot distinguish a proxy-degraded qualified call from intentionally authored qualified XML without provider provenance; that is a product policy choice rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Approve qualified-only history scrub
options.body: Accept the provider-signature rule and merge the branch so qualified degraded markup is removed from both delivery and persistence.

options.title: Limit cleanup to visible delivery
options.body: Preserve the current persisted-history behavior while using the shared visible-text sanitizer to prevent users from seeing the leaked markup.

recommendation.title: Approve qualified-only history scrub
recommendation.body: Accept the provider-signature rule and merge the branch so qualified degraded markup is removed from both delivery and persistence.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the most detailed technical context for the proposed distinction and can clarify the observed proxy contract, though final policy approval belongs with a repository decision-maker.
